sources.citation: Capell, A. 1968. What do we know of Tasmanian language? Records of the Queen Victoria Museum, Launceston 30.

sources.note: Original Tasmanian (tasm1247): p.3 'In Tasmanian it is extremely hard to make statements about syllable structure or stress, because it is not possible to listen to living speakers'; refers to Schmidt 1952 pp.114-121 on syllabification and accent.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section gives vowels /a i u/ + diphthongs ay, uy and a consonant chart, clusters pr/tr/kr, Taylor's critique; no statement about stress.

sources.note: Respelled pronunciations (e.g. 'Kunanyi.. pronounced ku nah nyee', 'Larapuna.. lah rah pu nah') with no stressed-syllable marking; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre. 'palawa kani, the only Aboriginal language in lutruwita today' (program web page), Internet Archive copy 2018-08-04 and 2024-04-28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes how the sounds of each word are reconstructed by comparing recorders' spellings via IPA and written in a custom-designed palawa kani alphabet; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Taylor, John Albert. 2006. The Palawa (Tasmanian Aboriginal) languages: a preliminary discussion. MA thesis, University of Tasmania. 288 pp. doi:10.25959/23206187.v1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About the ORIGINAL Tasmanian languages (tasm1247), not palawa kani: sec. 7.3.3 (p.138-139) and p.160-161 read Walker's/Robinson's/Sterling's/Cunningham's diacritics as stress marks -- 'the marks indicate the regular stressing of the first element in words, and generally speaking either no stressing of any of the remaining elements, or at best secondary stressing'; sec. 7.9 Stress and Accenting (pp.257-259) endorses Dixon's 'initial syllable is generally stressed' for Palawa, quotes and rejects Crowley & Dixon 1981:413 ('any syllable except the last can bear stress'), and concludes the diacrit…

sources.citation: Roth, H. Ling. 1899. The Aborigines of Tasmania. 2nd ed. Halifax: F. King (language appendices).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Original Tasmanian: reproduces Walker's vocabulary with macron/breve marks said 'to indicate accent rather than quantity' (Appendix E); no rule stated. scanned of the appendix is poor.
